summary: My apartment is in the Jordaan, one of the oldest neighbourhoods of Amsterdam - a perfect location to get a feel for the city. It's a cozy one-bedroom within walking distance to several sights, bars and restaurants. You're right in the centre of everything, but in a quaint, quiet street.
space: You can't beat this location. It's right in the beautiful, historical centre of Amsterdam. As soon as you step out the door, you're in the Jordaan with ample choice of restaurants, little boutiques and one of the oldest movie theaters in town. It's a short walk to the canals, the Anne Frankhouse and to the commercial centre. Easy access by public transport, with trams and buses right around the corner, and Amsterdam Central Station just a 15-minute walk away. The apartment is in a building built in the 1800's which has been classified as a historical monument (though thankfully renovated in 2006) in a charming, quiet street. You get a taste of Amsterdam's history, with modern comforts and amenities.

neighborhood_overview: The neighborhood: The Jordaan is one of the oldest and most charming neighborhoods in Amsterdam. You can wander around and explore at leisure, away from the throngs of tourists lining up for Madame Tussauds. You're in the middle of things, right by the famous canals, close to all the sights, there are authentic bars and cafes on every corner, quirky vintage stores. In short, this area oozes 'gezelligheid'. There is no English translation for that, so you'll just have to come visit and experience the Jordaan for yourself!
notes: This apartment is a wonderful home away from home. It's small though, or, as I like to say: cozy! It really is most suitable to two friends or a couple. Doesn't work for large gatherings, parties, or young kids (because of a downstairs neighbor who is quite sensitive to noise...)
transit: Public transit links are right around the corner. It's a 15 minute walk from Central Station, and there's a bus and tram stop about 3 minutes away, with trams running further into town or to Central Station.
access: Guests will have access to the entire apartment during their stay, and will have their own set of keys to go in and out as they please.
interaction: The place is all yours during your stay, I'll make myself scarce :-) Of course, your hosts will always be available by phone or e-mail if you have any problems or questions. There will also be someone to meet you at the apartment when you arrive, to give you the keys and make sure you're all set.
house_rules: Please note that homes in Amsterdam are generally small and built closely together. It is important that guests do not inconvenience the neighbours by talking loudly, playing loud music, or wearing heels on the wood floors.  If you're looking for a place to stay for your drug and alchohol filled weekend in Amsterdam, this is probably not the place for you. This would work well for responsible travellers who have experience with staying in someone else's home and respecting the place.  This is a strictly drug, smoke and pet free apartment. Excessive alchohol consumption will also be a problem (see point about the neighbours above).  If any complaints are received from the neighbours about noise or inconvenience during your stay, you will be asked to leave.  In short, if you treat the apartment & the neighbours as you would your own, there should be no problems!

neighborhood_overview: Amsterdam East is a hip and upcoming area close to Amsterdam’s city centre. Within walking distance there are lots of nice coffee bars (BRU Coffee, Rum Baba, Maxwell, Koffie in Oost), excellent and even famous restaurants (Rotisserie, Mama Dough, La Vallade, De Kas, Wilde Zwijnen, Michell’s Inn), 2 cinema’s (Studio K, Kriterion) and some of Amsterdam’s best bars and clubs (Hotel Arena, Roest, Volkshotel!). The museums are also close by. Within walking distance you can visit the Artis Zoo and the Hermitage. A 10-15 minute bike ride will take you to the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and the Amsterdam Stedelijk, the Red Light District or to the newly opened EYE: film museum and Cinema on the northern bank of the IJ River.  If you like to cook your own food, there are 4 supermarkets nearby. The apartment is also located in between de two largest markets of Amsterdam: the famous Albert Cuyp Market and the Dappermarkt, both a 5 minute bike ride away.
transit: It's really fun to rent bikes to get around the city. Amsterdam is really safe;  going out at night-time by bike is not a problem. If you like cycling, we could also recommend some good cycling routes to explore the beautiful areas surrounding Amsterdam.  Note that parking is quite expensive in Amsterdam (min. 3 Euros per hour / 18 Euros per day). If you come by car, we suggest that you drive to our house, offload your luggage and then park the car just outside the city. From there it’s a 30 min. walk or a short metro ride back to the apartment. You can rent bikes in many places, the closest location to our house is the Zwarte Fietsen Plan. host_about:
Rob Hoogerwerf (Apeldoorn, 1977) is een pionier op het gebied van persoonlijke ontwikkeling en NLP. Hij staat bekend als een uitzonderlijke communicator en buitengewone persoonlijke coach & trainer. Zijn stijl is interactief, uitdagend, leuk, diepgaand, intuïtief, onderhoudend en informatief. Rob is een ondernemend type, met oog voor kansen en empathie voor anderen. Hij is kwaliteitbewust en werkt doelgericht. Als communicator bewaakt hij het overzicht en processen zorgvuldig. Door zijn ervaring heeft hij affiniteit met vele sectoren.

Rob heeft zich ontwikkeld tot internationaal gecertificeerd NLP trainer en is opgeleid door o.a. de mede-grondlegger van NLP Dr. John Grinder, maar ook door innovators als Carmen Bostic St. Clair en Michael Carrol. Daarnaast heeft hij zich ook ontwikkeld tot NLP Master Coach en volgde hij de hoogst beschikbare NLP coach opleiding in Nederland op het gebied van NLP-coaching. Deze opleiding is als zodanig geaccrediteerd door de NVNLP, ABNLP, VIV Nederland alswel de NOBCO.

Rob heeft zijn sporen verdiend in het bedrijfsleven. Hij volgde een studie Management, Economie en Recht (MER) in Amsterdam en is werkzaam geweest bij (inter)nationale organisaties als L’Oréal, Capventure, UNLP, Sysmex en Vendex KBB op zowel operationeel als managementniveau.

Na zijn carrière in diverse marketing en sales functies als Area Manager in de cosmetische industrie, National Account Manager in de chemische industrie en Sales Director in de Design & Gift industrie besloot Rob om zich te specialiseren op het gebied van persoonlijke en zakelijke ontwikkeling en werd hij werkzaam als trainer en coach.

In zijn vrije tijd is hij te vinden in de fitness school, in het bos en soms op de tennisbaan. Hij houdt van natuur, reizen en lezen. Vrienden, familie en Lola de hond zijn erg belangrijk voor hem. Rob is tevens oprichter van Kontrast

The area is called Spaarndammerbuurt, which is a nice old working class neighboorhood that has developed a lot over the recent years. neighborhood_overview: Like Amsterdam, our neighborhood shares cultural diversity. There are more than 200 nationalities living here in Amsterdam which makes it like living in a big hostel.  Our place is far enough out of the Center of town to enjoy the "morning hush" but close enough to get to the movie and get popcorn by bike or public transport if it starts in 20 minutes.  We are in the heart of 3 amazing Parks, Vondel Park, Rembrandt Park and Sloterplas so if you are travelling with a dog or a runner this is the place to stay.
notes: We love having guests and sharing our city and home.  We are not sticks in the mud but if you have come to Amsterdam to party it will be best you find a place closer into town.  This is a quiet neighborhood and we like our neighbors.  Coming in late is never a problem, in fact we do it all the time staying out to see live bands (one of our passions)  but we do ask you honor and respect our home, surroundings and neighbors.

We will show you how to use the coffee machine and where the tea kettle is.  We can always make room in the fridge if you need to store anything and Ann will make you a full breakfast, which is included in the price and is happy for you to share any other meal with us if you want to expirence a Dutch/American collaboration . Let us know when you book of any allergies or dietary needs.  We certainly don't want to serve you anything that will make you sick.  She also packs yummy picnic baskets or a  box meal for the train or bus ride home at an additional cost.  Also we can teach you how to use the washing machine and dryer priced per load.
interaction: How much you want to interact with us is up to you.  However Peter is a native Amsterdamer and quite a history buff so he is the ideal tour guide and advise giver.  He is happy to share his knowledge with you and even happy to guide you on a private tour customized to your needs if he is available. He also speaks fluent German, Spanish, English and Dutch of course.  Currently Ann works from home so most likely will be here for your coming and going.  If your flight gets in before check-in time just let me know and we will see if we can come up with a time that will be more convienent for you.

I am Ann who moved from Texas via California (Lived there 10 years) to Amsterdam all for the love of a Man in 2005. We met in a Austin hostel back in 1993 and became penpals and wrote handwritten letters back and forth for 9 years. neighborhood_overview: Oud Zuid is one of the upscale area's of Amsterdam. It's known for its tree filled lanes, beautiful, spacious houses, lovely restaurants and fancy shops. But also of course for the Vondelpark, that lovely, green haven in the middle of Amsterdam, which is less than 5 min from the B&B. And, not to forget, the Museumplein, where you'll find three of the most famous museums in the world: The Rijksmuseum, 't Stedelijk museum and the Van Gogh museum. It's only a leisurely 15 min walk away (passing by one of the fanciest shopping streets in Amsterdam - the Cornelis Schuytstraat) or 5 min by tram. The Leidseplein (which is where the city centre starts seen from us) is 10 min by bike or tram. And thé most famous shopping street of Amsterdam (if not Holland), the PC Hooftstraat, with shops as Tiffany, Louis Vuitton and Chanel is also in Oud Zuid, next to the Museumplein. Always nice to wander around a bit....
transit: Tram 2 stops practically in front of Petit Paris (nearest stop is 'Amstelveense weg' or else 'Emmaplein'). It will take you to the Museumsquare, PC Hooftstraat, Leidseplein & Leidsestraat, the canals, Damsquare and finally the Central station (or the other way around of course). Besides tram 2 there are several other trams and buses that stop close to the B&B.
access: The suites are situated in the souterrain of the house. Guests will have the keys to the house & their suite, so they can come and go as they please. We, my family (husband, two teenage sons and Doedel, our happy dog) and I live in in the house as well, on the main & 1st floor, so we'll share the front door. This area is mainly private, but you can always knock on the door if you have any questions or whatsoever. The house has a garden, which you are free to share with us.
interaction: Me or my husband, Hein, will welcome you upon arrival, and will tell you all about the B&B, the area and all the nice, cool, touristy and/or off the beaten track places to go to in Amsterdam, including tips on how to get around (by foot, bike or tram). During your stay we will help in any way we can to make your visit to Amsterdam a wonderful one.
host_about:
I'm the owner of B&B Petit Paris. Besides the B&B I have my own interior decorating company. I used to work for some of the leading magazines in the Netherlands (o.a. Living, LINDA.), which gave me the opportunity to share my love for 'finding places'; restaurants, shops, markets, and of course the little unknown places off the beaten track. I can now hopefully share that with you. If you have any questions at all, about the B&B or Amsterdam, please don't hesitate to drop me line.

Hope to welcome you here soon!
Dascha

space: Our gallery/studio is based at OT301 in Amsterdam. The size of our gallery is 5,20 by 7,75 metres. OT301 used to be a squat in the Dutch city of Amsterdam which is located on Overtoom 301. EHBK has now bought the building which is used as a multi-media alternative cultural centre. The building is an old film academy and was squatted in 1999 by a group of artists. It is used in a range of ways, including as a venue for music and films, artists workspaces, a bookshop and an 'organic cultural kitchen' (a vegan restaurant) called De Peper. The building is a very lively place.During the weekend there are often performances, bands and parties in the big studios of the OT301 building, this can be quite noisy but also very interesting. So if you are looking for a quiet hide away, the AWA HOTEL might not be what you are looking for, but if you are looking to find open, interesting, vibrant people this is the place to be.

This Amsterdam neighbourhood is famously diverse with over 100 nationalities represented. While still the best neighbourhood to choose from a wide selection of ethnic food, more high-end bars and restaurants have come on the scene to service students and young professionals. neighborhood_overview: Considering you're in Amsterdam, the neighborhood is quiet. Almost no cars pass the street. But at the corner there is a nice neighborhood bar, where you can drink your coffee on the terrace, or drink a beer at night, watching the game. On walking distance there are quite a few nice restaurants, with good food for a reasonable price (not to be found in the center!). The supermarket is only a 100m. away, and a park only 2 minutes walking. And the best of it: only 15 minutes to the inner city center!
transit: From the airport you'll take the train for 10 minutes, and then the tram for another 10 minutes. The tram stops right at the door (well... 20 meters further actually). The same tram takes you to the Jordaan, Dam square, Museum square, Leidseplein, etc. and all within 15 minutes. Perfect bike distance, so get a bike and peddle around! Night bus also stops in the vicinity, so if you don't feel comfortable biking after a beer or two, just take public transport. Upon arrival (or whenever needed) I'll explain all the best routes to and from the center or other places.

Or do you want to get out, but don't know what to do? I can and will always help you around in the city, whether you look for a club or a restaurant, or a bike or tickets for a museum. Don't waste your time looking around, I'll show you so you can enjoy your stay in Amsterdam!

host_about:
I live in Amsterdam for half my life, stuck around after studying. Can't think of a better place to live! In the Netherlands that is ;) I'm lucky to be able to live and work in a fantastic apartment in a fantastic city, and I love travelling myself, so I'm happy to share my city with others! While staying at my place, I'll either show you around, or you'll just ignore my tips and advise and explore the city by yourself. I love music, going out, eating and travelling, so I can show you the restaurants in town, great clubs to go out, nice pubs to chill and drink a beer, venues to go to for a great concert or help you out with the do's (bike around) and don'ts (fall of your bike) for a tourist in Amsterdam

neighborhood_overview: Our house is situated in the "Watergraafsmeer", a lake that was "ingepolderd" in 1629, wich means drained of water by windmills to create "land". It is a real polder, where a serious  sea battle took place before it became the lowest lying land in Amsterdam. For a long time it had only farms and "country houses"for rich Amsterdammers, of wich only the Frankendael estate remains, now a very nice park. At the end of the nineteenth century  the expanding city of Amsterdam poured over into the Watergraafsmeer, and nowadays it has many different quarters in a very diverse mixture of architectural styles.

neighborhood_overview: What makes our neighbourhood special is the diversity of people. There are many artistic people living in this neigbourhood, actors, artists, different cultures, expats, young and old. We all get along quite easily. The atmosphere is easy going and open. There are many nice café's and coffeecorners nearby, as well as all the necessary shops (walinkg distance), and nice restaurants. The Vondelpark is only 5 minutes away from our house, as is the Leidsesquare and the Jordaan with it's famous canals (one of the best shopping areas of Amsterdam). You can walk to the musea: Rijksmuseum, van Gogh, Stedelijk, and otherwise take the tram to go anywhere else, the tram stops at a few minutes from our house. The liveliness and typical Amsterdam atmosphere is only a few meters away, but you will definitely also enjoy the tranquility of our house, garden and surrounding areas after a busy day in Amsterdam.
notes: Our home is a real family home, with a cosy and domestic feeling. We ourselves are easy-going people, and we hope you'll see that our house is breathing that same atmosphere. Feel comfortable, with respect of our belongings, but feel free to 'live' in our house. We have two very lovely cats. If you like we leave them. They need to be fed at least once a day, and go in and out themselves. It is no problem to let them stay with family so you don't have to take care of them if you don't like to.  Our house is an appartment in a big, monumental building. We live with our neighbours like it is a small village. Each of us lives in the building in private, but we are attentive of our neighbours.
transit: Different trams have stops near our house, but you can walk to most of the highlights of Amsterdam.
access: You can use and enjoy the big garden, which is partly private, and partly for communal use. Nevertheless it is always a very quiet garden, with mostly one or two neigbours enjoying the sun and the tranquility of this special place.
interaction: We would like to communicate mostly by email, and we would like to mail a bit forth and back to get to know each other a bit. We will not be in the house during the rental period. We zijn allemaal dol op Afrika: de uitgestrekte, kleurrijke vlaktes, de dieren, de mensen, het klimaat. Onze reisbestemmingen zijn heel divers, van primitief tot luxe, van drukke steden tot desolate woestijnen. Onze kinderen kunnen zich -net als wij- thuis voelen in allerlei verschillende situaties en hebben dan weinig nodig om veel te genieten.

Verder luister ik graag naar muziek: het pianospel van mijn dochter, golden oldies op de radio, wereldmuziek, pop..... en ik zing graag mee!

The latter has existed for over 100 years as a charming city forest, highly recommended for a leisurely stroll or picnic. host_about:
Hi I'm Femke. Together with my husband and dog I live on the Viator, our converted cargo ship. We both work a full time job. Our dog, Sjem, comes form the shelter but got used to the boatlife pretty soon. He likes keeping a close eye on all the activities going on in the harbor. He won't be able to come near the apartment. During the weekends there is always some painting work to do up and around the boat. We also love walking the dog in the Westerpark with a take away coffee in one hand and a fresh croissant in the other ;-). 

We purchased the boat in 2010. The first 4 years we lived on the apartment that now is the Airbnb apartment. During these 4 years we have saved money and were busy getting the licenses to be able to rebuild the cargo space into a house. We really love living on the water. It gives a great sense of freedom. It will let you experience the elements (sun rises, full moon, storms, beautiful clouds) yet you are very close to the centre of one of the most beautiful cities in the world. 

We are happy we can share the experience with you and hope you will enjoy the environment and Amsterdam a much as we do. 

Hope to see you around!
Femke

neighborhood_overview: De Pijp district is one of the most cosmopolitan and vibrant districts of Amsterdam. Formerly a working class quarter built to ease the overpopulated Jordaan in the 19th century and to house laborers, de Pijp as we Amsterdammers know it today is without doubt a melting pot of cultures and nationalities. You can indulge yourself for hours in Amsterdam’s lively Latin Quarter, with its colorful mix of cuisines, terraces and convivial cafés. From the beautiful landscaped gardens of Sarphatipark to the famous Albert Cuypmarkt street market, De Pijp oozes beatnik flair from every angle. Our apartment is on a quiet residential street in the New Pijp, around the corner from Van Woustraat, where you will find cafes, restaurants, supermarkets, local shops and great tram connections. The heart of the city and RAI convention centre are both reachable in less than 15 minutes by tram.

host_about:
We are a family of three, living on our ship in Amsterdam. If you have any special requests for your stay or need information on places to go, eat, drink, please do not hesitate to drop me a line. I will try to answer you as best as I can to make your stay as pleasant and comfortable as possible.

Our ship was build in 1899 and originally used for transportation. Many years ago it was transformed into a beautiful houseboat and now located in the centre of Amsterdam. The Haarlemmerstraat, which was called the best shopping street in The Netherlands in 2012, is 300 meters away. Central Station is within walking distance.
Our ship is docked in the oldest part of Amsterdam: Prinseneiland / Jordaan. 
We have a quay, next to the ship, where you can relax in the sun, till late in the evening. We also have a fire pit at the quay, so you can extend those lovely nights....

We have a big kitchen, with dishwasher, microwave, freezer, etc.
The livingroom is big as well, we have a television, wifi, WII and a wood stove.
In the front of the ship is one (large) bedroom with a big bed for two large persons and in the back of the ship is a bed for two persons and a bedroom with a build-in bed (1.40m).
We have a bathroom with a bathtub and shower.
Washing machine is also available on the ship.
We have two cats. They are both lovely and will stay on the ship.

We have a natural fence of plants around the water, so it is quite safe for little kids. But we also have life vests for the little ones, which is advised.

The ship is docked and not able to sail anymore, so you don't have to be afraid of waking up in the middle of the canal ;)

All in all a great opportunity to experience the Dutch live on a houseboat!

host_about:
Hi! My name is Gloria! 
I am hosting the renting out of our own house in Amsterdam and I normally am the one who plans the holidays abroad. We are a family of 4: me, my husband Amir and our 2 kids Noah (5) en Maiya (4).

We like to use Airbnb because on holiday we like the comfort of an apartment to relax and play in and where we can make some breakfast or lunch for ourselves. Especially when we travel with the kids having an apartment for ourselves and getting a local experience we see as an advantage. Staying in someone's house makes us feel less " touristy" and it gives us the opportunity to connect and understand better the different culture of a country and how people live and feel. 
With renting out our place we can feel we can do the same for others.

Both me (Dutch) and Amir (Pakistani/Brazilian) have lived abroad for many years. We met eachother in New York, US. We settled down in Amsterdam about 10 years ago. We would describe ourselves as very open people that are interested in other people, cultures and way of life. We do like a sense of comfort when we travel. 

We look forward to many other interesting traveling experiences and interesting people to meet!

neighborhood_overview: My apartment is situated in the famous SoHo like area ‘De Pijp’. A neighbourhood with countless cafés and bars, breakfast, lunch & dining options from around the world. You will find an amazing bakery with sunny terrace at the corner for a wonderful breakfast experience. It’s just a 2 minute walk to the famous Albert Cuyp market and the beautiful Sarphatipark and It will take you no more than another 15 minutes to stroll to the Leidse square and Museum quarter where you will find the van Gogh museum, Rijksmuseum, Stedelijk museum and the Concert Hall. Even the RAI Congress Center is really nearby as is the connection to the airport (train station RAI or Amstel). Bus and tram stops are just around the corner, these will take you pretty much to any place in the city. The possibilities of getting around in amsterdam are truly endless…..But the best and most flexible way to discover the city is of course by bike, which can easily be rented (cheap) at the bicycle shop around the corner Supe

transit: You can rent bikes at the bike shop around the corner. The way to discover Amsterdam as a local. host_about:
Hi! I'm Annebel, 31 years old and I work as a member of the editorial committee at a public broadcaster in the Netherlands. I am currently working on a documentary series about (similarities between)  football and ballet and a documentary about dance music. 
I have my own apartment in Amsterdam West and live at my boyfriends half of the time, who lives in Amsterdam as well.
I love to travel and explore the world and it's different cultures. My last travels were to New England (Boston/New York), Vietnam, Scotland, India and Rome. Still deciding my next destination.
I'm a bit of a running geek and like to do yoga, fitness and spinning occasionally. Good food, good wine, good coffee and good chocolate make me happy, especially when shared with good friends!
I wish I could find the time to go to the theatre, cinema, musea and concerts more often then I actually do. Also, I love to go out and dance. Jazz or techno and everything in between, whatever suits the occasion!

Opposite of our house lays the Vondelpark, the most famous park in Amsterdam with it's terraces, cafes and playgrounds. neighborhood_overview: The museum district, like most of the attractions in Amsterdam are mostly within walking distance- Rijks, Stedelijks & Van Gogh museums are only a 10 minute tram ride or 15 minute bike ride.   Anne Franke house is just a 5 minute walk away.  The train station is a 15 minute walk or 5 minutes from the tram. The district's borders are formed by the Lijnbaansgracht, Brouwersgracht, Prinsengracht and the Passeerdersgracht. host_about:
Welcome! 

My name is Corina, Dutch citizen in the historical city center of Amsterdam. After I have travelled the world quite a bit, Amsterdam is the place where I raise my son (now 12!). Besides of being a busy mother, I am an entrepreneur and yes, we have a b&b on the ground floor of our fantastic house in the Jordaan, the vibrant heart of Amsterdam. A special b&b as we do not serve breakfast. Dutch regulations that is and we kind of like it that way. We strongly recommend that you go out for breakfast... as our neighbors are specialized in making you a good breakfast. We guarantee you will never be hungry during your stay in Amsterdam. 

We love happy caring guests who love to explore Amsterdam by foot as all city highlights are closeby. And we collect special traveltips in Amsterdam for our guests....  Our location is our very best asset! We strongly encourage to experience Amsterdam like it is... like we love it. Happy strolling around from highlight to highlight. We are Amsterdam and the place is Amsterdam. It is as it is. However, if something is disappointing or missing, please let us know so that we can help you and/or correct it. 

Sometimes we get interesting requests like is there a kitchen? No, sorry but we offer coffee & tea facilities in the room and it comes with a small fridge. If you need plates, just ask please. Another question: Can we use your wash machine? No sorry, but there are laundry services in the city, plus we do not like it if you wash clothes in the bathroom and hang them in the room and garden... as you might understand. Or: Can we use drugs in the garden? No, our place is smoke and drugs free. However, during your stay you can smoke a couple of cigarettes in the backside of the garden, but if your plan is to smoke there every hour, better find another place as I provide my son with a smoke and drugs free home. And many more questions like what is a lit jumeaux? Can I have an early check in? In general that is not possible BUT you can store your luggage in our corridor on arrival and take the key. We will try to get the room clean & ready asap for your after 11 o clock. Same for the day of departure: you can store your luggage in the corridor and pick it up by the time you are ready to leave Amsterdam. Easy going & as flexible as we can. 

My son & I love to travel and we love to explore new places. Mostly in and around Amsterdam but also abroad. Besides of working hard, we have an active lifestyle and we like to sport.  I run (mostly Vondelpark), I swim (Marnixbad and sometimes open water) and I play basketbal like my son. We love to do outdoor sports as well, like hiking, canoeing, skiing, etc. 

My son has bought two bikes to rent out to guests but so far the adventure got stuck and the bikes are in the corridor for repair. Soon he will boost his entrepreneurial plan..

We absolutely love welcoming happy guests and we do love the airbnb concept. You pay the price that is quoted by AirBnB and  we pay all the taxes necessary to be able to host you and we like it that way. No hidden costs. Well, except the bikes by the time you can rent them...

Enjoy the hustle and bustle of the city center one day and take a bike ride towards the traditional villages of Holland such as Monikkendam the next.  We are located at 'Meerpad' which means lake path.  The small lake is enjoyed by kids for swimming in summer and skating in winter. On the other side we have the Vliegenbos (a city forest) perfect for your morning jog! We will provide you with all the information you need to make the most out of your stay.

interaction: We have just moved to this house, for reviews on me as a host, please check out my other listings.
house_rules: Our house is made from wood. So please be extra mindful of not setting it on fire. No big rules, just enjoy it like it's yours, care for it like it's yours.  I don't charge a cleaning fee, I just trust you to just leave it as you found it. Smoking is allowed, just take it outside. Really nice people live in this street, mostly young families. So go and party all night, and then opt for a silent disco once you head home. Oh! It would be AMAZING if you would be into watering my plants, but I will not use it against you if you don't :)
host_about:
I love unexpected smiles, I love not wanting to finish a book, I love that special moment when you take the first bite of something really delicious and your face gets all crazy, I love getting lost in foreign cities while pretending I live there, I love hearing stories from cab drivers, cashiers and concierges because they make your anonymous day so personal, I love it when you admit something silly and then the other person starts to laugh and admits to the same thing and you feel so normal and connected, I love taking naps after lunch, I love giving out energy and ignite something or someone, I love understanding new bits and pieces about myself and the world, I love dressing up on a dull tuesday morning, I love meditating and yoga, I love uncool second hand stores with all their junk and gems, I love to create new projects, ideas and plays, I love to hang around the house with friends and so much more.

My husband Jurre and I love renting out our home because it provides us with a reason to travel :)  We have truly enjoyed seeing our home through foreign eyes, appreciating it anew when we are back in the city.

Oh and some stats too of course:  32 years old, freelance actress. I studied Acting in NYC and I also have a  Master's in Communication from the University of Amsterdam. I also completed a Yoga Teacher Training in Rishikesh India but that’s just for fun ;-)

neighborhood_overview: Bon en Lommer is a vibrant family neighborhood in Amsterdam - it is a real melting-pot with families from all over Europe and the globe. Our little corner is a peaceful paradise, a great place to escape the busy city center, yet only 10 minutes from the city center by tram or bike! We are located on the Erasmus park, where you can hear summer concerts, bar-b-que alongside the neighbors, or enjoy a drink at cafe Terrasmus. If you are traveling with children they will love the little urban-farm and the great playground right in front of the door. We are located about 5 minutes walking from Bos en Lommerweg - a vibrant shopping street with grocery stores (including a natural-foods grocery), bakeries, fruit and vegetable stands, cafes, delicatessens, a pharmacy, bookstore, florist, and everything else you could need. notes: We ask that you kindly water the plants... Especially on warm summer days. If you are traveling with small kids let us know their age, and we can leave out some toys, books, etc.
transit: The best way to get around Amsterdam is by bike. If you are up for biking (it's very fun and easy with all of the designated bike lanes that are separated from car-traffic) then you will find yourself in the historic center of the city within 10 minutes. You can also reach everything in Amsterdam very easily by public transportation. Trams 12 and 14 pick up just 3 minutes walk from our front door. Tram 7 and busses 18 and 21 pick up about 5 minutes walking distance from our apartment. Within 10-15 minutes you are in the historic center. Trams run until midnight, but even if you stay out late in another neighborhood, we are just 30 minutes walking, or a short taxi-ride from the center. Amsterdam is a great walking city, it's very flat and the weather is mild, plus you will get to see so many of the details that make it so unique!

There are various horse stables and riding schools in the area. Extra housekeeping is available on request. We will arrange this with you on arrival. If you will be arriving or leaving much earlier or later than our normal check-in and check-out times, please let us know; we can be flexible if necessary. neighborhood_overview: Amsterdam is so small, every part of the city is within close reach wherever your place.  Love the diversity of my neighborhood, 'De Pijp'. The apartment itself is set right along the Amstelriver. On the other side there's great places to take an evening meal or stretch your legs for a walk. Takes about 15/20 minutes and your right in the center of the city. Plenty of small streets , odd and interesting little shops, especially near the Albert Cuypmarket wich is about 10 minutes walk from the house. More info and tips will be provided on location of course.

One note of Major Importance this appartement is not suitable for small/young children as there are many stairs so they cannot be left unattended. neighborhood_overview: It's cozy and it's getting more and more young dwellers. New shops are popping up together with bars and clubs: Podium Mozaik (on Monday's nights the offer salsa courses apart from the weekend highlights), The Zurich (local pub restaurants in Mercatorplein), best Thai in Amsterdam west Kratiam Thai and others. With tram 7 and bus 15 you can then commute to any spot in the city with just one change. host_about:
My name is Laila,

Born and raised in Amsterdam,  traveling the States for work for the last couple of years.

This lovely low- maintenance city is a metropole within a village; it combines the thrill and diversity of serious metropoles with the cosy and safe qualities of a village. It's the kind of city of love and it's the kind of person I am; I love the thrill and the quiet. 

I have always been fascinated by storytelling and political campaigning and managed to make a living out of that fascination. I used to work in political campaigning but switched to journalism in 2016. As a free lancer, I travel the United States a lot and touch base in Amsterdam about 6 months a year. 

Furthermore I love cinema, basketball, cooking, dining, wine, springtime and long walks. With the ones I love, of course. In 2016, I started surfing and have taken every chance ever since to catch waves.  

I started booking with airbnb in 2011  and knowing the joy of staying in a great and homy place  decided to be part of the sharing economy all the way and share my place and knowledge of this city with like minded travelers around the world in 2014. I really do believe the sharing experience adds to the any stay, anywhere. My home is not a holiday rental - I care to share it with travelers who enjoy the sharing and local kind of travel and treat a home that same way.

Being firmly secured to the canal wall, the ship hardly moves. What sets this houseboat apart are its huge roof terrace (you won't find another one this big in the old city centre) and its second floor, overlooking the Amstel. The upper deck boasts a large open kitchen, the lower deck contains the living room, creative space, cozy library with fireplace, the master bedroom with a kingsize bed (2.10x1.80), the bathroom with shower and jacuzzi and the toilet. For accommodating more than 2 persons, there are two additional queen size beds (2.10x1.40m) available in the living room (behind the chalk boards). These are very comfortable beds, but they are not located in a separate sleeping room. The total living area is around 100m2, the roof terrace is around 25m2.

notes: Limitations - There is a legal limit of 4 persons maximum on the boat, at all times.  - The boat is the best place for throwing a party in Amsterdam, but unfortunately that is not allowed, nor is anything loud or annoying for the neighbors. - Strictly no pets and strictly no smoking. transit: Getting there and around - Car: you can park on any public (paid) parking spot around the boat. Subway, tram, bus, and taxi stations are all within 5 mins walking distance.  - Taxi: a cab from Schiphol airport will take around 20 mins and should be just under € 50. From Central station or Amstel station a cab will set you back around € 15 in 10 mins. - Public transport: from Schiphol airport you can easily travel to Amsterdam Central station (or Amstel station) by train in around 15mins. From there take any subway line to Waterlooplein subway station. Follow exit Nieuwe Herengracht and then Hermitage museum signs, as soon as you are on the Amstel you will see the Skinny Bridge (around 5 mins walking distance). - By car: Amsterdam is hard to navigate without navigation system. No one really knows what the name "De Pijp" stands for. Some people say it owes its name to the long and narrow streets that resemble pipes or to the infamous gas company, the 'Pipe', which used to supply energy to the area. Formerly a working class quarter built to ease the overpopulated Jordaan in the 19th century and to house labourers, De Pijp nowadays is a melting pot of cultures and nationalities. In De Pijp 144 nationalities live together. It is one of the most popular residential, shopping and entertainment areas in Amsterdam. The Dapperbuurt is known for the second largest market of Amsterdam after the Albert Cuyp Market. It has been a designated market street since 1910. It is possible to turn the couch in the living room into a double bed, that way the apartment can accommodate 4 people, but keep in mind it is meant for 2 people, so living there with 4 might be tight.  I also want to mention that the living room does not have dark curtains and is located at the street side (no cars, only pedestrian and a tram line during the day). Generally it is not noisy though, but if people want to check in with more than 2 people, keep this in mind for those who will sleep in
neighborhood_overview: The area, the Indische buurt, is a lovely vivid area, but nice and quiet at night. It's located close to the center, it's just about 10 minutes by tram or bike. In the neighborhood you can find several nice cafes, restaurants and parks. There is also a small cinema right across the street and you can find a known market on walking distance, called the Dappermarkt. A famous beer brewery, Browerij 't IJ, is not too far away either! By bike or tram it's just a matter of minutes (2 stops) and i guess it's about a ten minute walk. Especially in summer their terrace is crowded and a lot of fun! A little bit further away is the zoo, Artis. If you take the tram 14 to the city center you will pass by Artis.
transit: Public transport is right in front of the door! Tram line 14 will take you to the city center in just about 10 minutes. Do keep in mind that tram 14 does not take you to Central Station! Central Station you can easily reach by bus 22 (also very close to the apartment) or by train, from Amsterdam Muiderpoort, which is a ten minute walk from the apartment. Several other public transport lines are available in the area too, depending on where you want to go. From Schiphol airport you can take either a taxi, a shuttle or a train (which will take about 30-40 minutes). I can give you more detailed information after your reservation is made.
access: Guests have access to everything in the apartment and the garden and are allowed to use all equipment. Please be careful of course and please let me know if anything breaks or stops functioning.
interaction: During your stay I won't be in the apartment, it's all yours. I will only be there during check-in and check-out. host_about:
Hi! I'm Carry, a 33 year old woman from Amsterdam, The Netherlands. I love to travel and I take every opportunity I get to go abroad! I studied Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at the University of Amsterdam. Lately I've been particularly interested in Food Anthropology and the debate about poverty, development and food. The subject is still quite new to me, but I hope to work in that field one day.

Besides studying (actually learning in general) and traveling I enjoy being with friends/people, eating, fitness, biking, parks, walking, baking sweets and talking!

In 2010 I have traveled through South America as a backpacker together with my sister for about 10 months and fell in love with the continent, especially with Argentina and Buenos Aires and I have been going back yearly. 
In 2016-2017 my sister and I lived and traveled in New Zealand with a working holiday visa, so that was another big adventure :)
During my holidays I would like to offer my apartment in Amsterdam to fellow travelers. I would like to participate through this website both as a host and a guest.

In my profile I said I speak Spanish, because I do understand most of it. I'm far from fluent though, especially my speech isn't good at all haha!

In case I am abroad either my mother Regien or sister Belle will be your host and handle both the check-in and check-out. In that case their contact information will be available to you after booking.

If you have any questions feel free to ask, I'll be happy to answer :)

Amsterdam’s elegant Oud-Zuid (Old-South) was developed over a century ago as a cultural gateway to the city, at the tip of what was previously a boggy polder. It’s home to Rijksmuseum, Stedelijk Museum, and Van Gogh Museum – all of which exhibit the highlights of Western art. A lot is going on here and recently it was elected to be one of the top three hippest places in the world to live. It's 10 minutes away from the city center and 10 minutes away from the 'polders' , the dutch countryside. Nearby my house you can find a small grocery, a bio shop, a nightshop, 3 super markets and on wednesday-friday and saturday there's a big open market in walking distance, selling local products. Bars and restaurants are well presented, you will find a map at my place and the location where to find these. A brand new swimming pool is just around the corner and it's a beautiful starting point to explore the city or the Dutch country side by bike.
notes: I have a bird in my house, it's a small harmless yellow singing canary in the living room. Wakes up when the sun rises and starts to sing, this can be a little bit early if you want to sleep longer. There's an easy solution to keep her quiet, a blanket can be put over the cage in the evening and you can take it away again when you wake up. I just ask not to leave the blanket too long covering the bird, and not to play with the bird, cause she's easily stressed. Food is available for refill the containers if necessary. Keep an eye on the water container and please from time to time, fill it up. Most of the times it will have enough food and water for 3 days.

If with the car, there's free parking in my street and its save to park here. Bikes can be rented in Noord.

neighborhood_overview: Our house used to be part of the Olympic Village during the 1928 Olympics. The Olympic Stadium is right around the corner. This part of Amsterdam is called Oud-Zuid (Old South) and is within walking distance of all the finest culture Amsterdam has to offer, such as Rijksmuseum, Stedelijk (modern art) museum, Van Gogh museum, concert building, Vondelpark, etc. It is a quiet residential area, yet very easy to get to the busy city centre and has all the conveniences that you need at walking distance: shops, supermarkets (regular ones, but also organic ones), a very good French bakery, cheese & wine shops, news stands, restaurants and bars. Most important for us personally are the many green public spaces and children’s playgrounds.
notes: MINIMUM STAY: 5 nights. MAX NR GUESTS: 4 people (preferably families with/without kids). AVAILABILITY: Please check our calender. There are cheaper alternatives (Park & Ride at Olympic Stadium for 8 euros per day for a maximum of 3 days), but often very busy (long queues when parking is full, as then it is 1 in - 1 out) .
transit: From Amsterdam Schiphol airport: taxi (20 mins, 40 euros) or bus 397 (20 mins and stops from a 5 minute walk to our house, approx. 6 euros single ticket). Public transport is around the corner. It only takes about 20 minutes to get to the historic centre with its canals and 30 minutes to the Central Station. You can easily walk or cycle everywhere. IMPORTANT NOTE FOR CAR PARKING! Parking is in the street (usually there is a place right in front of the door), but bear in mind that it is PAID parking from 09:00-21:00 EVERY DAY except Sundays. Day tickets cost 21 euros. There is an alternative: Park & Ride parking underneath Olympic Stadium for 8 euros per day, but that is for a maximum of 3 days and needs to be in combination with public transport pass and registered trip from city centre when you pick up your car again. If you need any (other) directions we will help you. We will also provide you with a map.
access: The whole apartment (we won't be there), minus 1 bedroom that we will lock to store our personal stuff in order to give you your own (cupboard) space. neighborhood_overview: We can't think of anything that is not completely wonderful about the neighborhood. It is very alive, with lots of little cafes and delicious restaurants from all over the world, but the apartment itself is situated in a quiet and friendly street, where a lot of people know each other. Kids use it as a playground.  Besides the daily Albert Cuyp market with fresh fruit, veggies and fish, there are two supermarkets around the corner and there are wonderful boutiques and unique shops. You can choose to have a nice stroll to the Stedelijkmuseum of contemporary art, the Rijksmuseum with the astonishing Nachtwacht from Rembrandt van Rijn, fall in love at first sight with the Straatje van Vermeer or discover that Van Gogh's landscapes are even much more beautiful than when you see them in books. All museums mentioned have been renovated impressively.
notes: The place is very clean and cosy. You will have a perfect holiday but it is also very suitable when you are on a business trip.
transit: You can get to Dam square from the Pijp within ten minutes by tram. Another two minutes and you are at the Central Station. De Zuid-As and A10 are easily accessible by car, bike and public transport. Public transport to all parts of the city is within walking distance.

interaction: The place will be all yours from the minute we hand you the key. But of course we will be at your service anytime.

neighborhood_overview: De Pijp is vibrant and very much on its way up. As can be expected of an area that is centred on the nation’s most famous outdoor market: Albert Cuypmarkt, near to the Heineken brewery. This Amsterdam neighbourhood is famously diverse with over 100 nationalities represented. While still the best neighbourhood to choose from a wide selection of ethnic food, more high-end bars and restaurants have come on the scene to service students and young professionals. Further east along De Pijp there is the Van Woustraat, a former fast food strip, there are now several of the city’s more highly regarded restaurants. But perhaps most representative of the area is Bazar, a former church on the Albert Cuypmarkt that has been reinvented as a funky North African café/restaurant. host_about:
I love making music, gardening, riding my bicycle and turning my house into a beautiful and cozy space. Together with my husband Jang, I love to receive guests and sharing all that makes our spot such a wonderful place to live in. I love the colours in and around our house.

I teach music to very young children (I used to be a kindergarten teacher) and was able to turn my music hobby into my profession. I love classical pieces, but also folk and world music. We love visiting small music festivals, especially in summer.

When I stop moving around and take the time to sit down and read, I usually pick up a psychological novel. We try to minimize watching TV, but if we do watch it, we choose travel and housefinding programmes. Going to a movie with a friend is another one of my regular treats.

We eat food from various foreign cultures, such as Turkish, Indonesian, Mexican, Libanese, Thai, etc. Of course we also love to travel, together or on our own. Portugal, Czech Republic, France, Norway, Turkey, America, Aruba, Lebanon, Syria, South-Africa. These are some of the countries we have visited. Ik like camping as well as staying in a bed and breakfast. A hotel is fine for a couple of nights, but not my favourite stay on a holiday trip. I like to travel by train or bicycle.

My life's motto would be: sharing my good fortune and happiness with others.

The neighborhood is called Oud West and is a very nice mix of population and facilities. The area has seen rapid gentrification so  very good new bars, restaurants and coffee places keep appearing (and disappearing). Although the street and neighbourhood are very lively, we are yet a few minutes away from the really noisy part of town.... so you can sleep well and enjoy a quiet, comfortable space!

Do not use taxis unless you have to: they are expensive and the scale and structure of Amsterdam makes traveling by car impractical.....

Anne Frank is a block away - you can here the same beautiful chimes of the Westerkerk that Anne Frank recorded in her diaries.   Dam Square and the Palace are a short stroll away.

Here you can also go sailing, windsurfing, kite surfing and paddle boarding. There is also a nice harbour.

But sometimes (and this is rare) check in / check out times can overlap when leaving guests have a late flight and arriving guests are coming early. If my place is already booked, I can highly recommend this private apartment also listed at airbnb and has great reviews :) https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/28126549 Also it's possible to book my experience to see this newly developed area by boat. You have easy access to public transport with a tram stop 6 minutes walk from the houseboat (it runs every 6-10 minutes). The tram will bring you to the inner city centre like Central Station within 12 minutes. It is approx. a 30 minute cycle to the inner city centre from the houseboat but it is also possible to take the bike on the tram with you. The night runs the whole night from 12.30 to the city centre and back that takes 30 minutes.  If you come from Schiphol Airport it is 15/20 minutes by train to Central Station, from there you take Tram 26 (Ijburg written on the front) and stop at tram stop Steigereiland (which takes 12 minutes). neighborhood_overview: neighbourhood: Our house in located in the popular eastern docks area with lots of interesting modern architecture. Water truly surrounds you everywhere in this neighbourhood. Most of the area was build in the 90s  and is well known for its architecture. Students from all over the world visit all year round to see the unique JAVA-island and Scheepstimmermanstraat. There are some nice restaurants, the hip Lloyd Hotel with a lovely outdoor terrace in the back and some very special shops on walking distance.   The street itself is quiet and friendly. The large playground is great for playing soccer with your kids. Locals swim in the water of the IJ that surrounds our residential peninsula on 3 sides. Although it is not officially allowed it's an excellent way to start the day!
notes: city of Amsterdam The city offers many nice parks, great restaurants, a lot of unique shops, the Anne Frank House, Rijksmuseum (with most famous Nachtwacht by Rembrandt) Stedelijk Museum of Modern Art, Van Gogh Museum, the famous Canals and picturesque  17th Century Centre, Rembrandthuis, Red Light  District, Blijburg (the hippy beach on IJburg), and of course many hidden treasures.
transit: Amsterdam is a compact City, especially the 17th Century centre. From our home the city centre is a 10 to 15 minute bike ride. Biking is highly recommended in the summertime. Tram 10 and 26, busses 48, 22, 65 are at approx. 8 minute walk from the house.  Parking your car is expensive but easily available in our street. For longer stay we recommend parking at P+R for aproximately 4 Euro a day. It is just 1 stop by tram.  You can travel with tram 26 from the Central Station (train station). It would take about 30 minutes in total .  Or take a taxi when you arrive with a lot of luggage. It cost me 15 Euro's last time I did that.
access: All the space behind the front door on the shadowy patio is yours! See description.  The front room at the street will sometimes be occupied by the owner. It has a separate entrance.

host_about:
This was a truly unique experience to stay on a houseboat. I grew up in Amsterdam but never had the opportunity to stay or even visit a houseboat. I stayed here for 10 days at the end of April and was very fortunate to be blessed with great weather. My stay was excellent and the houseboat contributed a large part to that. It is located in one of the best locations of the city: next to the Jordaan and close to the Westermarkt (with Anne Frank house). It is very quiet on the water even though the city is hustling around you. Sitting outside, looking out over the water is a great experience. Weekends the canal is a bit busier with lots of small boats coming through but it create a unique atmosphere that you will not find in any of the hotels. The houseboat itself is unique so it is hard to describe, it is not small, but it does create an intimate atmosphere. I can see it would be great for a romantic stay (even though I stayed alone Lachebekje (zwart-wit)). The layout makes that the sleeping part is separated from the kitchen/living part even though there are no doors between the sections. The bed is excellent, the shower strong and hot, the kitchen fully equipped, lots of books to read and music to play. But most of the time you will be sitting outside enjoying the view of the canal and the sounds of the city. The nights and morning could be a bit chilly but heather worked just fine. I would recommend the houseboat to anyone who would like ta truly unique Amsterdam experience.
May 2014 Werner CFO Amazon

Next to cosy bars, stylish cafes and restaurants you will find independent concept stores - even a cupcake bakery and a cat cafe. The coffee roasters 'White Label' and cookie bakery 'Koeke Bakkers' have their shop/cafe combination around the corner. Grocery stores as Albert Hein and Dirk are close by - even  Surinamese, Asian and Turkish supermarkets where you'll find more special ingredients. The shopping area  Oostpoort is within walking distance and public transport  (tram 9) taking you to the heart of Amsterdam is around the corner. There are a number of beautiful parks in this area (Oosterpark and Park Frankendael). In the surrounding neighbourhood you can find everything that makes your weekend break or longer stay in Amsterdam comfortable and enjoyable. In Amsterdam you can find a windmill near my accomodation, in the neighbourhood of the Dappermarket. At Waterloopplein (Waterloop Square) near the Flea Market you can rent a bike at Mac Bikes (on the route of tram 9). You also can rent bikes at Amstelstation or Muiderpoort station, both are in the vicinity of my apartment. You can explore Amsterdam on your own or Mac Bikes offers a daily Amsterdam City Bike tour, led by a guide who takes you along the best sites in Amsterdam. - Music (especially latin music, it reminds me of home).
- Dancing salsa
- Travelling
- Food! Especially my mom's (the best cook ever), Italian, Asian and Haagen-dazs ice cream. :-)

- Italy, especially Tuscany. Words cannot describe how beautiful this country is. It was love at first sight. Great people, great food, great wines, great architecture and history.
- Spain. I love the people, ambiance, tapas and siesta. Plus a beautiful language.
- Florida. The sunshine state. Experience the USA in a different way.
- Aruba, One Happy Island. Beautiful white sand beaches. Sit back, relax and enjoy.
- Curacao. Beautiful island with lots of Dutch history.
- Berlin, Germany. You can just feel the history in your veins when visiting this city. Enjoy the street art and open minded people. Not to forget the underground nightlife.
- Prague, Czech Republic. Beautiful, nice and cozy city.
- Morrocco. Enjoy the great food, great hospitality. Don't forget to visit the Hammam.

- Cuba

- Australia
- Mexico
- Colombia
- Brazil
- South Africa

neighborhood_overview: The Nieuwmarkt-area is one of the oldest in Amsterdam, where Jewish and Chinese cultures left their cultural marks and where commerce thrived, symbolised by the former castle-like weighing station of 'De Waag', right in its centre. There are markets and activities almost every day. The area offers a lot of cafés and restaurants. On the west side you'll find the old seamen's area 'De Wallen', better known as the 'Red Light District', on the east side are the small and quiet streets of the 'Lastage' area, home to shipping warfs and warehouses centuries ago. The Nieuwmarkt area has an active political history, where tension rose high in the late seventies, as protest was fierce when hundreds of houses were demolished to make way for the new subway line, running right under our house.
notes: • The CAFÉ nextdoor has a terrace that can be noisy until late in the evening, especially on warm summer nights. People who are sensitive to this can find it annoying. Windows have thermopane glazing and when shut prevent most of the noise entering the room. Alternative ventilation can be obtained by opening the room door and back windows in the stairway. • We have a CAT, but it will never enter the guest room. • Guests can borrow our BIKES if they want, but because the saddles take ajusting and the brakes are of the back-pedaling kind, it might be smarter and safer to rent bikes around the corner. • The STAIRWAY is according to modern Dutch norms. The width is 75cm/30inch minimum, depth and height of the steps are normal. There is a handrail. Still, new guests will have to get used to it, and some people may experience the stairway to be steep or narrow. • On the ground floor is a STUDIO for group work and when activities are going on (once or twice a week), guests will be asked to us
transit: From the airport of Schiphol trains take 15-20 minutes (4,30 euros) to reach Amsterdam Central Station, starting point of almost all tramways and bus lines. From there it's a ten minute walk to our house. You can also take the subway (lines 51 or 53) to the first stop, called 'Nieuwmarkt'. There, choose exit 'Nieuwmarkt' to emerge 30 yards from our house. Parking a car in the neighbourhood streets is troublesome and expensive, just like using parking garages nearby. Using a car in the city is not practical anyway. Best option is to park at a 'Park&Ride', like 'Zeeburg-2'. That costs only 1 euro per day, including a obligatory tramway ticket to the centre of town. More (Email hidden by Airbnb)

neighborhood_overview: The Boreas is located on a private jetty on the authentic old shipyard the NDSM-wharf in Amsterdam North. You are only 9 minutes away from central Amsterdam by ferry.  The NDSM area emerged the last five years as one of the hippest and most creative neighborhoods in Amsterdam. In the summertime there are festivals organised every weekend, and in the winter there are all creative and cultural events in the huge warehouses. The location is awesome - you can take the ferry for free wich leads you directly into the centre. Still there are very cool bars and restaurants right next to the boat. Two minuter wal from the boat you will find Cafe Noorderlicht, an organic restaurant that already had sustainability and bio-products before it became a trend. In the evening they often have bands. Slightly further you will find Plek, a restaurant built from shipping containers, with great food and good music. At the departure site of the ferries there is fine bakery Brood.
notes: There is a possibility to park your car not far from the boat, it's free. We can explain this by arrive. It's not aloud to have party's on the boat or use extreme alcohol or drugs!
transit: There is a 15-minutes-ferry( free), that will take you directly to Amsterdam Central Station. An other ferry in 9-minutes takes you to the stunning area Jordaan with the fameus '9 straatjes'. When you come with car you can park it in the living area not far from the boat. There also exists another ferry at a 15 minuter bicycle ride distance from the Buiksloterweg NDSM ferry to Central Station. This goes every night all night long even 12 minutes. You will therefore always get home, no matter what time it is!
access: You have the whole boat for your own. We are there when there is a group, we live separate from the group. So when there is something you want to know about your stay, we are available.
interaction: We will receive you by arrive and explain how it is to stay on a boat. If there is a need for advice during your stay on our boat than I'm available. You can contact us to get free information about all the options for a stay with us on board.
house_rules: We are proud of our beautiful boat and expect from guests that they treat this as their own house! With respect! We do not aloud extreme alcohol and drugs use in the boat! No smoking!
host_about:
Hello I'm Grietje!

Together with my husband Henk we have this beautiful ship. It's an old ship from 1897. In the old days this boat had cargo on board and sailed across the sea from Holland to Denmark and Sweden.

Nowadays we are sailing in the Summer with groups of people on board who have a sailing holiday and in the winter we are moored in the beautiful city of Amsterdam. We stay here on one spot. I like to have people on board who enjoy being together.

 I am a woman of the sea and everything that has to do with water has an enormous attraction on me! I love life and take care of myself by eating healthy food, walking in nature with our dog and practice yoga, and sail in the summer of course!

Carpe Diem!

So when you want a nice and special place in the World city of Amsterdam, come on board and feel at home on our ship! We are pleased to welcome you!

Your hostess Grietje

neighborhood_overview: The Eastern Docklands used to be the old harbour of Amsterdam in the 19th and first half of the 20th century. Lots of warehouses are still left but a great deal of the area has been rebuild around 1990 with lots of modern architecture. From our place you can enjoy watching the ships go by on their way to Germany and Switzerland. It's a quiet neighbourhood and only 15 minutes to the centre. A large shopping mall and some cafe's and restaurants are within walking distance.
notes: We have two very nice dogs, (working) border collies, but we will keep them on our floor. If you are allergic to dogs, please take your precautions. And we have two grandchildren, a girl of three years old and a boy of just one year. We take care of them two days a week.
transit: From Schiphol Airport: take the train to Central Station. From Central Station: take bus 48 direction Borneo Eiland. The bus terminal is located at the back side of Central Station, direction IJzijde. Take the escalator to go to the first floor and walk to section C. Hop on the bus and get out at the last bus stop, RJH Fortuynplein. Walk the rest, some 300 meters direction east and ring the doorbell at 348. If you like to bike around Amsterdam, you can rent bikes almost on every corner. Good place to rent a bike is near our house. Just ask and we will explain how to get there.  If you come by car we advise people to park at P & R Zeeburg. (Parking fee in our street is 3,50 euro an hour). Check out their website at iamsterdam. From there: tram 26 direction Central Station 1 stop, to Rietland Park. Change there to bus 48 direction Borneo Eiland (you have to walk 100 meters to this busstop in the direction of the shopping mall) and get out at the end stop RJH Fortuynplein.
access: The ground floor is yours. The second and third floor is ours.
interaction: Depends on you.  We're perfectly willing to help you discover Amsterdam. Do not hesitate to ask us anything, we'll be around quite often. If we are, come and have a drink upstairs.

host_about:
After having lived for years right in the hectic centre of Amsterdam we decided to move to this quiet old harbor area.  Maike used to work as a book and paper conservator and Caspar is still active as a journalist. 
The things we like: Taking a dive in the IJ in front of our house to wake up. Have an espresso afterwards as a reward. Going to the Bimhuis - a famous jazzcafe - in the evening to listen to Ibrahim Maalouf (yes, you can listen  his music on Spotify). Making nice meal, having a good glass of wine, watching the ships go by.... 
And of course, helping you trying to figure out what museum to visit, where you can find to best and cheapest restaurant,  what beer is best (Heineken or Grolsch), if the Red Light District is safe to visit at night (YES), and where to find the hottest  place in town (right across the IJ).

Frankendael, now turned over in a great restaurant (do eat lunch on their wonderfull terrace in summer) on the Middenweg, is the one example that has survived. There's a wonderfull garden and town park adjacent. You don't even have to go to the citycenter to spend a wonderfull time in Amsterdam: the Watergraafsmeer (and the other eastern parts of Amsterdam) is a very popular neighbourhood, full of hipster cafés and trendy restaurants, a list of which we will provide. You can look for great architecture at the nearby Indische buurt, and the Eastern Islands. neighborhood_overview: A formerly working-class neighbourhood, today de Pijp is home to a multicultural community and the city's largest market. The colourful sights and scents of the Albert Cuypmarkt are sure to delight and the area teems with charming ethnic restaurants, cosy brown cafés and trendy bars and terraces. Be sure to visit the streets behind the market for an over the top cake with your coffee at De Taart van m'n Tante. Not into sweet? A Suriname sandwich from Tjin's will explode in your mouth. Or bring your favorite take-away, perhaps from the Pizzabakkers with a cold bottle of Prosecco, to the local Sarphatipark
notes: The Hidden House is central but local and provides a friendly priced family foothold for city explorations.
transit: Two tram stops only minutes away from The Hidden House allow you to reach any point of interest fast and easy. RAI station/convention centre 10 min. Central Station 12 min. Museum Quarter 14 min. Dam and Palace 8 min. From Schiphol Airport to The Hidden House by public transport takes ONLY 35 MINUTES, door to door. neighborhood_overview: The wide canal outside the front windows is the "highway" for bigger boats passing Amsterdam.  Everything from traditional wooden ships to coastal barges, river cruise boats to kayaks, yachts to house boats, goes past the window.  Although it's directly next to the centre, this is a 'real' neighbourhood, with Amsterdammers going about their daily lives, not a tourist bubble.  There are five markets within walking distance, selling food, organic produce, fabric and crafts, respectively, on different days of the week.  Two supermarkets, a bakery and other shops for practical needs within five minutes walk - including of course booths selling fresh cut flowers (a necessity of Dutch life!). And several bars, cafes, restaurants within a few minutes.
notes: Price includes healthy breakfast. Delicious dinner (vegetarian or fish) available by arrangement. The building is wheelchair accessible, and the apartment is suitable for persons with mobility limitations. Mostly, check in and check out times are flexible - except to accommodate another guest. However on some occasions you'll need to pick up the key at a local business, and let yourself in. Occasionally, I may be traveling, and you'll be staying here alone. In that case, you have access to the whole apartment except my bedroom, and I'll leave a good supply of breakfast items for you.
transit: You can walk to many attractions within 15 minutes or less.  Excellent public transport if you need it. Several trams and buses within three minutes' walk or less. From the airport to Central Station it's about 20 minutes by train, and from CS to my place it's less than 10 minutes by bus.  Trains and buses run very frequently from early morning until midnight.  Paid parking on the street outside - generally good availability.  Cheaper parking at multistory carpark three tram stops away. (You won't need your car while in Amsterdam).  Cycle shop with bike rentals on the corner.
access: You have access to the whole apartment except my bedroom.  Crisp clean sheets and nice fresh towels provided. You have your own room with direct access to bathroom. There is a separate additional toilet.   The very big living/dining room is also at your disposal - stylish dining table and two comfortable sofas.  Large TV with cable, WIFI access available.  You're welcome to all of this, including if you want to work at the table. The kitchen is available to you most of the time, too. I rent only one room, so you are sharing the facilities with myself and occasionally also my boyfriend.
interaction: I love hosting, but as a frequent traveler, I also understand that there are times when you may just prefer not to interact much.  I'm available, but not in your face. I am happy to provide you with information, insight or suggestions about exploring Amsterdam, or to let you discover this lovely city in your own way. I have maps and guide books if you want them.  I work from home much of the time, but my office is separate from the living area.
house_rules: "Do unto others...."  - treat my place in the way you hope I'd treat yours. Please tell me if there's anything you don't like - I'd like to put it right if I can. No smoking in the building or on the balcony.  No drugs anywhere.  For the sake of my neighbours, please be quiet on the stairs and on the balcony after 10pm. Laundry by arrangement. So first a short story in english:

Hello everybody!
Introducung myself:

People call me extrovert, social and spontaneous. But the interaction with you, will also be influenced by your wishes and needs of course!
As an AIRBNB host I can prepare you tea or coffee with the dutch treat WARM SIRUP WAFELS, when you check in!
Travelling gives me a feeling of overwhelming freedom. I just love to travel around on our world with just 1 backpack. It can be challenging, interesting, exciting, squary, adventurous or horrible! I've been in more then 90 countries and my curiosity becomes bigger after every journey each year.
I also love to collect comic books, have almost 7000.
It means adventure and freedom to me.
When I read them I have the opportunity to travel around in my head.

I live in Amsterdam since 1988. At the moment in the cosey area DE PIJP.
In a beautiful apartment on floor 3 and 4, with a balcony and wonderful roofterrace, on stock 5. 

I have 2 rooms in this apartment which I rent for 3 guests. It is also possible to stay with 4 guests. But be aware: one of the  rooms is quite small for 2 guests. Check in time from 12.00 and check out time at 11.00.
These times are flexible ONLY when I do not have other guests checking in. Sometimes I have to work elsewhere. So let me know which check time you prefer. We have to sort out what the possibilities are. Some guests leave their luggage in my living room, during the check out day. Only possible if I do not need to work or have no outdoor apointments. And pick it up later.
Be aware that I'm living in this apartment, too. We do not need to share toilet and shower on floor 3. Because that is mine. You have YOUR shower and toilet on floor 4. We do need to share the use of the kitchen on floor 3. Although this was never a problem, I experienced after renting out for 3,5 years!
I am not always at home during your stay. Sometimes I need to work or have other apointments. You go your way. I will go mine.

MY HOUSE RULES:

The 2 rooms are available FROM 12.00 mostly. You need to leave the rooms at 11.00, because I need to clean them for the next guests. 

Please do not reserve the 2 rooms if you want 100 % privacy. Because I live in the apartment, too. We need to share the use of the kitchen. Where you can make yourself fresh coffee or tea. Or cook, bake or boil.

And use your own 2 fridges in your 2 rooms, please. Instead of mine.

Also be aware that the 2 rooms are very small! They do not have a lot of space to walk around.
The bathroom is comfortable.

And the 4 stairs are steep and narrow. Do not book these rooms if you have trouble climbing stairs. Not suitable if you come with heavy luggage or a baby! 

Take off your shoes before you enter my apartment. I do not want any shoes anymore in my apartment. To avoid dogshit and street dirt.

No loud noises in my house, corridor  or on the street. There are neighbours living on floor 1 and 2!

Help me to collect plastic and paper in different garbage cans in the kitchen.

Do not smoke in the apartment or in the 2 rooms.
You can smoke on the balcony or roofterrace.

No need to do any dishwashing. Just put your dirty plates or glasses etc in my dishwashing machine in the kitchen.

And enjoy your stay.

Maybe I will meet you when we travel around!
I wish you lots of inspiring journeys!
Maybe we will see each other in the future,
Kind regards, bye, adios, ciao, au revoir (Website hidden by Airbnb) Olaf

Hi, my name is Marcel and I live in the centre of historic Amsterdam on one of the most beautiful locations. In my home I run a Bed & Coffee with two rooms each with a private bathroom for maximum two persons per room. 

Besides hosting I work with artists as a curator. I'm a foody and spend much of my time cooking, going to the local markets and enjoy restaurants. If you need some advise where to go or what to eat please ask!

In my travels I visit and visited a lot of B&B's globally. Staying in a room in somebody’s home often felt I was staying with friends. Some of them became and still are dear friends after many years. 

In my home I offer my guests privacy. But please knock my door for questions or a chat any time and most likely we’ll meet on the terrace anyway ;)

Travelling and enjoying a city like Amsterdam is all about having a place where you feel comfortable at home and safe in a strange environment. And especially to have a very good bed, a warm shower and a good cup of coffee or tea. 

Live like a local and feel at home. 
This experience is what I try to offer my guests. 
Tot ziens in Amsterdam!

neighborhood_overview: The wide canal outside the front windows is the "highway" for bigger boats passing Amsterdam.  Everything from traditional wooden ships to coastal barges, river cruise boats to kayaks, yachts to house boats, goes past the window.  Although it's directly next to the centre, this is a 'real' neighbourhood, with Amsterdammers going about their daily lives, not a tourist bubble.  There are four markets within walking distance, selling food, organic produce, fabric and crafts, respectively, on different days of the week.  Two supermarkets and other shops for practical needs within five minutes walk - including of course booths selling fresh cut flowers (a necessity of Dutch life!). And several bars, cafes, restaurants within a few minutes.
notes: Building is wheelchair accessible and my apartment is very easy for anyone with limited mobility. Hand rail in small toilet. Paid parking on the street outside - generally good availability.  (You won't need your car while in Amsterdam).  Cycle shop with bike rentals on the corner. Boat rental just around the corner.
transit: You can walk to many of Amsterdam's attractions in 15 minutes or less.  Excellent public transport  it will take you to all other attractions within minutes.  Close by are two bus lines and two tram lines - it's five minutes by bus to  Central Station. Buses and trams run frequently throughout the day until about midnight.
access: Full apartment, including kitchen with oven/micro-wave, fridge, separate freezer, dishwasher.  Feel free to use the staples in the kitchen to prepare your own meals.  Large TV with cable, WIFI access available.   Washer and dryer in the apartment. Crisp sheets and nice fresh towels provided.
interaction: I will be away during your stay, but will give you all the information you need, and provide contact numbers for people here in Amsterdam, as well as my number.  Usually I try to leave you a 'breakfast starter kit' -  this depends how long I'm away for.
house_rules: "Do unto others...."  - treat my place in the way you hope I'd treat yours. No smoking in the building or on the balcony.  No drugs anywhere.  For the sake of my neighbours, please be quiet on the stairs and on the balcony after 10pm. Due to a regulation from my landlord, no tourists, only visitors to Amsterdam eg for study, work, family purposes etc. Please tell me if there's anything you don't like - I'd like to put it right if I can.
host_about: From Wales, lived in Canada, and on a houseboat in Amsterdam.  60 years old, female, non-smoker and vegetarian.  Careful and responsible guest..  My work is related to environmentalism. I sometimes travel with my partner, Hans Onno, who is 71 also a non-smoker and has a professional background in the cultural sector.
