I came to Amsterdam as a student and I worked with youngsters (8 to 19 yrs old) for the last two decades till 2014 ( in Dutch: Ik werkte met jongeren de laatste 20 jaar en verliet de jeugdzorg in 2014).

 At 44 I started my own Soap business in Januari 2015: De Amsterdamsche Zeepfabriek B.V. The Amsterdam Soap Factory, in Amsterdam. A social firm where we make organic handmade soap bars in Amsterdam, with whoever needs the place to get back to work and to be with others while doing that. Based on 500 years of craftsmanship of soap making as it was big business in Old Amsterdam in 1550.

Born in Utrecht, in the early seventies, I moved to Amsterdam in '89 to live and study here, and I never left. Except for vacations abroad: California, Australia, London-city and hitchhiking through Europe. Oh, and then New York and Joshua Tree. And Seattle, Austin, Savannah and Santa Monica.. Closer to home I love Vlieland in September, and the Netherlands for camping out.. 

I was so lucky to get a chance to live in this house in the '90's: a small floor just for me with everything I needed. Then two friends came to live with me and we got another floor. And then I got the chance to redo the whole house (2nd, 3rd and 4th floor) with my father Bram and his mate Dion in 2011.

My house is now the most beautiful loft-house in Amsterdam. You might want to have a glass with me at the rooftop. I'll think about it ;)

The floor you'll stay on used to be for me and my two stepchildren: they moved on. I like to use the rooms for guests: come stay, and help me pay off the bank :)

The construction of the Spaarndammerbuurt started at the end of the 19th century. The streets have been named after places situated in the West and northwest of Amsterdam. The labor houses had especially been intended for the dock workers, who worked in the ports nearby. The most famous buildings in the Spaarndammerbuurt are designed by Michel de Klerk, who devised labor apartments in the style of the Amsterdam School, situated at the Spaarndammerplantsoen. In the years around 1920, three of his housing blocks got constructed. The most striking design is 'The Ship’, located along the Zaanstraat. The houses were 'palaces for the workers’, because before no one really cared about the design of the worker’s houses. Also a post office was part of the block-system. This once working-class bastion was renowned for tight community bonds, radical politics and a love for drink and over-the-top sing-a-longs. neighborhood_overview: Just a short tram ride south of Centraal Station takes you into one of the most cosmopolitan and vibrant districts of Amsterdam. Welcome to de Pijp. For the eternally inquisitive, many will try to second-guess what de Pijp stands for but the truth is, no one really knows. Perhaps it owes its name to the long narrow streets that resemble pipes or to the infamous gas company, the ‘Pipe’, which used to supply energy to the area. Whoever or whatever is responsible for the name should be proud of the association. Formerly a working class quarter built to ease the overpopulated Jordaan in the 19 th century and to house labourers, de Pijp as we Amsterdammers know it today is without doubt a melting pot of cultures and nationalities. host_about:
We love this city, and at the same time we love to travel over the world. I was born in Amsterdam and Milan is originally from the South of The Netherlands. We have our own reasons for wanting to be in Amsterdam. The best thing about Amsterdam is that, by bike you move easy from one to the other place. With the first sun, people are catching the warmth, at the terraces or at the parks. (in front of our house)

We earn our living by doing our hobby. We have our own film production company in which we produce inspiring and adventurous documentaries. Our productions are screened internationally by tv broadcasters, as the topics or characters are interesting for an international audience. In contrast to our daily life, we also are very keen on activities outdoors. Hiking, camping all that kind of stuff. We love nature, and yes it is a cliche, but it reminds us of what is important in life. It helps to put things in perspective. 

The world is our playground and we enjoy going to other places and meeting new people, getting to know their routines, and traditions. We believe that sharing ideas and thoughts, only makes us smarter. 

In 2009 our first son Aiden was born, in 2013 his little brother, Kanoa was born.

Our motto is: live your passion.

A few steps from the apartment you can enjoy a wonderful park and a daily fresh market (Albert Cuyp). At the corner, you also have 3 supermarkets. You don't have to walk very far to enjoy all touristic attractions of Amsterdam. In the Pijp you can ensure you are having a real Amsterdam experience with locals. neighborhood_overview: Our neighbourhood Bos en Lommer has it all! There is a great variety of shops, deli's and restaurants on the main street 100m away and  three large supermarkets at the main market square. The neighbourhood has a big turkish community so expect great baklava and pastries, good grillrooms and lavish sunday breakfasts....  Outside our front door is a park with a big playground and children's farm. Yes a farm goats, sheep and even a giant ugly pig. I love traveling: from backpacking through Asia for several months to short citytrips; adventure awaits everywhere. As soon as I'm done with the hotspots and tourist traps (and that doesn't take too long), I love to explore a new city through the eyes of a local. That is where Airbnb comes in perfectly! Next to Amsterdam my favorite cities are New York and Berlin. My musical taste goes from alternative indie bands to house or disco dj's, with Radiohead's Thom Yorke being my absolute favorite musician. Considering the discipline in which I graduated you probably already guessed that I love films. And I will absolutely make a 30 minute detour for a good cup of coffee. summary: A typical Amsterdam canal house located right in the middle of the 19th century district "Amsterdam Oud-West". neighborhood_overview: The location is perfect. It is a short walk from“ De Hallen Amsterdam”, an official monument building where once the first electric trams in Amsterdam were serviced and is now a booming center for media, culture, fashion, food and crafts. Go for a pleasant walk through the picturesque streets in the neighbourhood and you will easily reach Museumplein, (Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Stedelijk Museum), Concertgebouw, 9 Streets, Leidseplein (Paradiso, Melkweg) and Vondelpark, all of them within 5 to 10 minute walking distance. Public transportation to and from the apartment is very close and convenient. Four different tram lines (3, 12, 7 and 17) stop around the corner to bring you in all directions possible.
notes: Besides the most known attractions, Amsterdam offers a lot more to discover and explore. In order to make your stay as enjoyable as possible, I put together a local guide with things you can do and see while visiting the city which you will receive at booking confirmation. And of course you can call me if you have any questions during your stay in the apartment. Be aware of our typical Amsterdam steep and narrow staircase. The apartment is on the 3rd floor and these traditional Amsterdam apartments don't have elevators ;-)

The area around is close to the natural park ‘Twiske’ where you can swim, walk, bike, picnic and relax. Officially this neighbourhood is called 'Kadoelen’. Opposite of our house is a nice Amsterdam ship wharf. They have electric silent boats that are for rent. The trendy NDSM wharf is only 7 minutes by bike and has many restaurants and café's. A monthly flea market and lots of events are happening at this wharf area. From there you can also take the free ferry to the city center. To bike to the ferry is only 8 minutes. It's a 12 minute boat ride to the central station.
notes: If you stay at our house you can use our bikes for free. We'll ask a deposit for that, you get this back from Airbnb after your stay.
transit: About the (public) transport options: From the central station you can go by ferry to the NDSM wharf, then 20 minutes by foot or 8 minutes by bike. Behind central station you can take bus 34 (to Buikslotermeerplein) and ask the bus driver to drop you at the Tjalkstraat. From there it's a 10 minute walk to our house.
access: You can stay with 5 adults and 2 (to 4) kids. We have two double bedrooms and 2 childrens rooms. Besides these beds we have 2 extra single mattresses available for children.
interaction: We won't be around during your stay but you can contact us when you've got any questions. We will make sure you will find all instructions about our house in a folder and some nice tips to explore Amsterdam. Our neighbours are  good friends and can give help if there problems with the house.

neighborhood_overview: Oud-West is a neighborhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands, roughly covering the area between the Overtoom, a major thoroughfare west of the city centre, and the parallel De Clercqstraat, a shopping street. The neighbourhood consists of two historically and demographically distinct communities: the Overtoombuurt in the south and the Kinkerbuurt in the north. Oud-West was a separate borough of Amsterdam until the 2010 borough reforms, when it merged with the boroughs of Bos en Lommer, De Baarsjes and Westerpark to form the larger borough of Amsterdam-West. Main shopping areas are the Kinkerstraat, De Clercqstraat, Jan Pieter Heijestraat, Overtoom, and Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. Oud-West is served by tram routes 1, 7 and 17 connecting the centre of the city with the western suburbs via the Overtoom (route 1) and Kinkerstraat (routes 7 and 17), as well as routes 3 and 12 running along the Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. neighborhood_overview: I'm living in this neighbourhood (Indische Buurt) for 4 years already and I love it!! The Javastraat is a 2-minute walk and here you find many authentic shops, restaurants, and boutiques. The famous Dappermarket is nearby as well (open monday-saturday 9h-17h) and worth a visit. Lucky me, the amazing Flevopark is a 5 minute walk away from my apartment, where you can lay in the sun, have a picknick or BBQ or have a nice walk/run. The Westerpark is a stone's throw away. What makes the Westerpark so cool is that it has much more going on than any other park. It has a cinema, a few restaurants, historical buildings, a jazz cafe, a bakery, a petting zoo, a kids pool area, a beer brewery, some great clubs and bars and also tv-studios. Ah, and it is the first park in The Netherlands with free WiFi!  In seven minutes walking you're in the best area of Amsterdam, the Jordaan with it's many canals! neighborhood_overview: Downstairs is a popular grand cafe (Walvis), you can have a drink and a meal or a bite there. If you sleep with the window open, you may hear some noise until closing time. Bar Mick at the opposite corner is also a nice place to drink and/or eat, it's one of my favourites. There's a big grocery store (Albert Heijn) at the end of the street (5 minutes walk). A stroll at the riverside (IJ) is nice, especially at sunset. The architecture in my neighbourhood is famous ('Amsterdamse School') and the 'Westerpark' is very nice to walk or run through or visit one of the cultural events that take place there. Both are within a 5 minute walk. The oldest cinema you find at the beginning of the 'Haarlemmerdijk' ("the movies"), it's very special! The Haarlemmerdijk and Haarlemmerstraat have also many shops and boutiques, you will love it. The famous 'Jordaan' with typical alleys, (canal) houses and markets is close by (15 minutes walk).
notes: Be aware that my apartment is at the 4th floor and there is no elevator. So you have to climb the stairs, it's a good exercise! But not suitable for people with disabilities. Early check-in (before 3 pm) or late check-in (after 7 pm) will be possible in most cases. Please let me know, there maybe an additional fee of 10 euro because of the extra costs I have to make. Late check-out may also be possible or you can leave your luggage upon departure.
transit: The busstop is in front of my door! There's a frequent service to the Central Station (7 minutes) or to the Station Sloterdijk (10 minutes). The public transport in Amsterdam is one of the bests in the Netherlands, you can travel by bus, tram (cable car), subway of boat. You can buy a cheap tourist ticket for 3 or more days at the Central Station. But of course walking or cycling around is typical Dutch and will bring you everywhere. You can rent bikes at several places (also in my street). Taxi fares are relatively expensive in Amsterdam, but I can order a taxi from the airport to my place for an attractive price (33 euro).

Within walking distance there are countless things to see and do. In no less than five minutes you can walk to the Dam square and the Royal Palace. The flower market, Anne Frank's house and the Red Light District are all close by. Want to do some shopping? The famous 'Nine Streets' and the Jordaan area are just minutes away. For the foodies among you, there are some outstanding restaurants to enjoy. As far as the location goes you really can't get much better in Amsterdam. And to finish it off: no more than three steps from the hotel is Tales & Spirits, recently voted Amsterdam's best cocktail bar! notes: Please be aware: we have a small elevator in the building which can be used to get to the room. However we ask our guests not to use it after 23:00. After this time you must climb four flights of winding stairs to get to the room, therefore it is not suitable for people with physical disabilities or people with general mobility issues. We don't have full-time reception staff so you will need to give us an approximate arrival time.
transit: If you’re flying into Schiphol Airport then the easiest way to get into the city is to take the train to Amsterdam's main train station (Amsterdam Centraal). The ride only takes about 15 minutes. From the station the hotel is about 10 minutes walk. We will send you more detailed directions once your booking has been confirmed.  Because of our proximity to the main train station, almost all of Amsterdam's tram lines are within walking distance.The trams will get you just about anywhere you want to go in the city. There are however also many bus lines close to the hotel which are useful for reaching areas outside the centre. Of course the best way to see Amsterdam is by bicycle! We will give you all the information you need to rent a bicycle, there is a very good rental place just around the corner.

Jennifer, Lisette & Heather
